Market Intelligence Briefing
subheadings: 🇺🇸 United States  Bullish  Fed on hold / cyclical upturn
🇪🇺 European Union  Bullish  ECB on hold / sub-target inflation
🇨🇳 China  Mixed  easing bias / weak demand
🇵🇱 Poland  Bullish  easing pause / fiscal risk
🧮 Earnings Pattern — What the Market Pays For
Cash today beats AI promises tomorrow
🔍 Underowned Themes — Active on X, Underweight in Portfolios
Oilfield services for the Venezuela reopening
Quality software after the AI purge
Crypto winter turns into a credit event
AI debt supply meets a weaker dollar
🔮 Anticipatory Positioning — Markets Pricing In Future Events
US–Iran: talks or a second carrier
$AMAT  results land into a fab-spending upcycle  ↑
$COIN  crypto winter hits the income statement  ↓
Micron & SanDisk / MU, SNDK  "the memory squeeze"
Gold & Silver / GLD, SLV  "the safe haven trading like a meme"
Bitcoin dip-buyers / IBIT, MSTR  "buying the winter"
body: Thursday, February 12 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: January payrolls rose 130,000 and unemployment fell to 4.3%, even as the benchmark revision cut job growth through March by 862,000. The January ISM manufacturing index printed 52.6% while December retail sales stalled: output is re-accelerating as the consumer cools, and the Fed has no reason to ease. Constructive on cyclicals, neutral on duration.

Rates & Curve: The 2Y closed at 3.52% and the 10Y at 4.18%, a 10Y−2Y spread of +66 bps — moderately steep, approaching the long-run average; over 20 observations the curve was little changed (2Y −1 bp, 10Y 0 bp, spread +1 bp), while over five observations the 2Y fell 5 bps and the 10Y 11 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-11). The 3M bill at 3.70% still yields more than the 2Y, so eventual cuts remain priced (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-11). The S&P 500 closed flat at 6,941.47, VIX at 17.65 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).

New / Most Important: Economists now expect the Fed to hold through May and worry that Kevin Warsh may prove too loose with policy. That makes Friday's delayed January CPI the decisive print: firm core inflation hardens the pause, a soft reading revives the easing debate.

Playbook ✓: Own cyclicals — industrials, energy, staples retail — over long-duration software, and keep duration neutral with the 10Y at 4.18% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-11). Add small caps only after a benign CPI on Friday. Cut risk if the 2Y climbs toward the 3.70% bill yield, a sign cuts are being priced out (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-11); add duration on a soft core print.

Macro Stance: Euro-area inflation fell to 1.7% in January and the ECB held rates, shrugging off the dip — the reverse of the US mix. Equity money is following: Europe and Asia led global fund inflows as investors cut US tech exposure. We are bullish on European equities, led by energy and banks.

Activity & Inflation: The constraint is the currency: EUR/USD closed at 1.1890, up 2.12% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11), importing disinflation and squeezing exporters. The DAX is down 1.7% over 20 sessions while the FTSE 100 is up 2.82% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11) — commodity- and bank-heavy indices are beating the export-heavy one.

New / Most Important: The STOXX 600 hit a record high as energy stocks surged while tech and financials stumbled, closing at 621.58, up 1.64% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). Dassault Systèmes' 18% plunge on its outlook shows the AI-disruption selling in software has crossed the Atlantic.

Playbook ✓: Own the STOXX 600 over the DAX; overweight energy and banks returning capital, underweight software, wealth managers and autos; hedge the euro on exporters rather than selling them. Change the call if EUR/USD extends its rally and the ECB turns to verbal pushback, or if inflation rebounds from January's 1.7%.

Macro Stance: China is running two economies: a deflationary domestic one and a buoyant technology-and-export one. Consumer prices rose just 0.2% in January and factory deflation eased more than forecast — better, but still deflation. Property and household credit are not recovering, while AI equities and the yuan are strong. We are Mixed: positive on onshore tech and the currency, negative on property, autos and consumption proxies.

PMIs & Activity: The official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in January, back below 50, so the producer-price improvement reflects anti-price-war discipline more than demand. Durable consumption is the clearest weak spot: auto sales fell at the fastest pace in nearly two years in January. Confirmation of a turn would need the February official PMI back above 50 and Spring Festival spending that holds after the holiday.

Credit Impulse: The latest full-year print is weak: 2025 new bank loans were the lowest in seven years, and Reuters noted that more policy support is needed. The feed carries no January credit print, so there is no evidence of a fresh impulse yet; January is seasonally the largest lending month, which makes the next release the key test. A rising share of household medium- and long-term loans would signal reviving property demand; short-term bill financing by companies would not.

Property: Property remains the drag. Shenzhen's government is drafting an $11.6 billion rescue package for China Vanke, according to Octus — a firewall against a disorderly default at a large developer, not a demand recovery. A package of that kind does nothing for sales or prices, and the feed carries no sign of stabilising home prices. Avoid developers and mainland-property-exposed lenders until monthly price data show the decline narrowing.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Beijing is spending on hardware rather than households: China will invest 5 trillion yuan in the power grid over the next five years, a multi-year order book for transformers, cable and grid automation. On trade, Europe is opening a door — Volkswagen's China-built Cupra Tavascan was spared EU duties on China-made EVs, a template Chinese brands will try to copy. Without a direct transfer to consumers, CPI stays close to zero.

Markets & Flows: The Shanghai Composite closed at 4,131.98, up 0.14% over 20 sessions, and the Hang Seng at 27,266.38, up 0.99%; ASHR is up 0.44% at 34.01, while KWEB fell 7.64% to 34.10 and FXI 1.94% to 39.47 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). USD/CNY at 6.9106 is down 0.96% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11), with the yuan at its strongest since 2023 amid a report on Treasuries. Flat onshore indices, weak offshore internet and a strong currency say foreign money is buying the yuan, not China platform equity.

New / Most Important: The AI rally has rotated to Chinese model developers: Zhipu surged 30% to lead Chinese AI stocks as a wave of new releases hit the market. The supply-side counterweight is memory — SMIC says the industry is in 'crisis mode' over the memory crunch, which can cap hardware margins even as AI-software valuations climb.

Playbook ✓: Own the currency and the AI-and-grid capex chain, not the consumer: prefer ASHR to KWEB, keep developers underweight, and express reflation through USD/CNY downside rather than equity beta. Upgrade consumption names only if the February PMI returns above 50 and January credit surprises up. ⚠ Divergence: the yuan at its strongest since 2023 contradicts a 49.3 official PMI and the steepest auto-sales fall in nearly two years — currency strength is a flow story, not a growth signal.

Macro Stance: Sanae Takaichi's landslide clears the path for tax cuts, and markets are reading it as disciplined reflation: stocks and the yen rose together. A Mizuho executive says the BOJ could hike as early as March and up to three times in 2026. That shifts leadership from exporters to domestic financials: Bullish, with a stronger-yen tilt.

Activity & Currency: The Nikkei 225 closed at 57,650.54, up 2.28% in the session and 7.66% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). USD/JPY fell 1.06% to 154.48 and is down 2.95% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). Japan's top currency diplomat says officials are not lowering their guard against FX volatility — a cap on disorderly moves in either direction.

Playbook ✓: Own Japanese equities tilted to banks and insurers, which gain from BOJ hikes, and trim yen-sensitive exporters; keep currency hedges partial. Add on a March hike signal that does not trigger a bond selloff. Cut if USD/JPY rebounds toward its 20-session reference of 159.1790 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-14), which would mean the carry trade is rebuilding.

Macro Stance: The RBA raised rates in February — its deputy governor said changes to 'three key facts' prompted the move — and Governor Bullock says the bank will raise again if inflation becomes entrenched. That collides with a softening household: spending fell in December after two strong months. A strong currency and resilient banks against a squeezed consumer make this Mixed.

Demand & Financing: AUD/USD closed at 0.7075, up 5.85% over 20 sessions, and the ASX 200 at 9,014.80, up 1.66% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). Banks are carrying the index: CBA's first-half earnings hit a record on market-share gains and the shares surged. Higher rates widen margins now but raise mortgage stress later, so the bank rally is a margin trade, not a credit-quality one.

Playbook ✓: Stay long AUD/USD while the RBA keeps its hiking bias; hold the major banks but take profits into strength; avoid rate-sensitive retailers and housing-linked names. Change the call if the next quarterly CPI undershoots or household spending falls again — either would remove the second hike and cap the currency.

Monetary & Activity: The NBP held rates in February (Bankier: 'Rates held — the NBP president comments'), and the MPC projects inflation in line with the target, leaving the key decisions for March (Business Insider Polska): easing is paused, not over. The weak link is fiscal — Fitch says Poland risks a rating downgrade if debt is not stabilised.

FX & Markets: USD/PLN closed at 3.5462, down 1.96% over 20 sessions, and EUR/PLN at 4.2182 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11): the zloty is riding euro strength against the dollar. EPOL is up 6.37% over 20 sessions at 38.39 and the WIG20TR ETF 4.43% at 67.85, led by Orlen (PKN) at 111.90, up 13.77%, PGE at 10.27, up 10.69%, and Pekao at 230.30, up 10.14% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).

Companies: Orlen shares are at their highest in years as commodities drive profits (Money.pl). KGHM rose 5.06% in the prior session to 320.00, while PKO BP is down 4.33% over five sessions at 91.94 and CD Projekt 5.11% over 20 sessions at 241.20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). Rzeczpospolita reports record billions flowing into funds as retail investors buy shares again.

Security & New Development: The event risk is the CJEU ruling on WIBOR-linked mortgages, which Bankier dates to 12 February and frames as a possible breakthrough for borrowers; a borrower-friendly verdict would reopen legal-provision risk for PKO and Pekao. Global capital keeps coming: a FedEx- and Advent-led consortium agreed to buy parcel-locker firm InPost in a $9.2 billion deal.

Playbook ✓: Overweight Poland via EPOL, led by Orlen and PGE; hold banks at neutral into the WIBOR ruling and add if it is bank-friendly; leave the zloty unhedged while the dollar weakens. Cut the overweight if Fitch moves the outlook to negative. ⚠ Divergence: record retail inflows into funds run against Fitch's downgrade warning — equity euphoria versus fiscal deterioration.

Narrative: Consensus still treats software as an AI beneficiary; the tape treats it as a casualty. XLK is down 2.4% over 20 sessions and Microsoft 14.09% at 404.37 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11), as AI-loser software stocks were overshadowed while hardware earnings jumped. The open question is per-seat pricing once AI agents do the work.

Reported: Cisco topped estimates but dropped 7% on a mediocre forecast, and French software maker Dassault Systèmes plunged 18%, on track for its worst day ever. Beats are irrelevant if guidance does not show AI lifting revenue.

EPS Upside Watch: Apple has the cleanest large-cap setup: AAPL is up 5.54% over 20 sessions at 275.50 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11), insulated by services and installed-base pricing. AI hardware, where the earnings jump is visible, is the other upside pocket.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Oracle and Palantir are down 22.31% and 24.18% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11): even AI-adjacent software is being sold indiscriminately — late-stage capitulation. Stay Bearish until a major software name raises guidance and holds the gain.

Narrative: Communication services split between ad and subscription platforms that monetise AI and capex-heavy giants that finance it with debt. XLC is down 0.13% over 20 sessions; META is up 5.96% while GOOGL fell 7.44% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11) after Alphabet sold almost $32 billion of bonds to fund AI.

Reported: Spotify shares jumped on strong earnings and subscriber growth — subscription pricing power is being rewarded even as software is punished. Disney is down 4.3% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).

EPS Upside Watch: Meta remains the upside candidate: its 20-session gain shows investors accepted its capex step-up, with AI-driven ad targeting the bull case. Spotify's price increases flow straight to margin, making it the cleanest beat-and-raise setup in the group.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Netflix is down 11.85% over 20 sessions at 79.62 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11): streaming is being de-rated alongside software rather than traded as a defensive. Mixed — own ad and subscription cash generators, underweight debt-funded capex stories.

Narrative: Financials should benefit from a firmer economy; instead AI-disruption fears jumped from software to brokers and wealth platforms. XLF fell 1.51% in the prior session and 2.75% over 20 sessions, with JPMorgan down 2.34% and Bank of America 2.78% on the day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). LPL closed 8% lower as the threat spread to financials.

Reported: Robinhood's stock plunged after Q4 revenue missed Wall Street estimates — retail brokerage is the most exposed corner to the crypto slump. The newsflow is about business-model risk, not deposits.

EPS Upside Watch: Goldman Sachs is the best-positioned large name: GS is up 3.43% over five sessions at 944.59 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11), with underwriting levered to jumbo issuance such as Alphabet's bond deal and trading levered to volatility.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The risk sits in credit, not deposits: Morgan Stanley warns the AI-led software selloff may pose a risk to a $1.5 trillion US credit market — lenders to software companies. Bearish until that contagion is priced.

Narrative: Consensus says oil is oversupplied, yet energy leads 2026. XLE is up 16.98% over 20 sessions, Exxon 22.93% and Chevron 13.39% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11), and Europe's record high was driven by an energy surge. The driver is rotation out of tech plus a Middle East risk premium, not the commodity balance.
Reported: TotalEnergies halved buybacks while keeping growth plans as low oil and gas prices weighed on profits. European majors are protecting balance sheets; US integrateds lean on volume growth.

EPS Upside Watch: Exxon and Chevron have the most volume leverage: Brent at 69.40 is up 6.0% over 20 sessions and WTI at 64.63 is up 5.69% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11), and at current output every sustained dollar of price gain drops to free cash flow.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The EIA forecasts lower oil prices in 2026 and 2027 due to persistent stock builds — the sector is rallying against the official balance. Bullish, but prefer US integrateds to payout-cutting European majors and keep trailing stops.

Narrative: Industrials are the physical leg of AI capex plus a cyclical recovery. XLI is up 6.6% over 20 sessions and Caterpillar 21.75%, including 4.4% in the prior session to 775.00, while the Dow closed at 50,121.40 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). The January ISM manufacturing index at 52.6% confirms the cycle is turning.
Reported: Caterpillar topped estimates as data centers boosted power demand — the clearest evidence that AI spending has reached heavy machinery and on-site generation.

EPS Upside Watch: Power-generation and electrical-equipment suppliers carry the most estimate momentum, with data-center load the common driver; Caterpillar's 20-session move says the market is still revising numbers up rather than pricing a peak.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Aerospace is lagging the cycle: GE is down 4.13% over 20 sessions and Boeing fell 2.61% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). Leadership has rotated from aero to power and construction equipment. Bullish; overweight power-gen, neutral aero.

Narrative: The K-shaped consumer is now in the numbers. XLY is down 5.19% over 20 sessions and Amazon 15.88% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11) after an earnings miss and $200 billion capex guidance. December retail sales stalled, so the sector has lost both its mega-cap support and its macro tailwind.

Reported: McDonald's beat estimates as its value push paid off — traffic is going to the cheapest credible offer. Tesla is up 5.48% over five sessions while Nike is down 5.96% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).

EPS Upside Watch: Value-led restaurants and off-price retail are best placed: McDonald's shows that value promotions can still deliver a beat when they win share, and chains with scale purchasing can fund them without guidance cuts.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Home builder stocks are breaking out with the best start to a year in a decade even as discretionary spending weakens — lower mortgage rates are beating the consumer narrative. Bearish on the sector, long builders as the exception.

Narrative: Staples are where the rotation out of tech is landing. XLP is up 8.99% over 20 sessions, Walmart 6.99% and Costco 3.84% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). The driver is relative safety plus pricing power at scale retailers, not a revival in branded volumes.
Reported: Ahold Delhaize shares jumped after growth in US online sales — the omnichannel-grocery formula that is also powering Walmart's re-rating.

EPS Upside Watch: Walmart and Costco: in a K-shaped economy the scale grocers can win share from both ends. Walmart's 1.63% gain in the prior session to 128.77 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11) shows the bid is still building after the payroll report.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Branded packaged food is not participating — retailers win the volume while brand owners lose it, which is why the rotation should be expressed through retailers, not consumer-products makers. Bullish on staples retail; avoid branded food until volumes stabilise.

Narrative: Health care is split between obesity-and-oncology growth and a managed-care margin crisis. XLV is down 0.31% over 20 sessions, but UnitedHealth fell 16.48% over 20 sessions and Lilly 8.3% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).
Reported: Molina shares sank 28% on a surprise Q4 loss and disappointing guidance, confirming that medical costs are still outrunning premiums for insurers.

EPS Upside Watch: Large-cap pharma with volume growth: Lilly's pullback leaves it at 1,015.21 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11), with obesity demand still the sector's main earnings engine and the pullback offering a better entry than at the highs.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Managed care looks cheap after the drawdown, but Molina's guidance says the cost cycle has not turned; the contrarian buy is premature. Mixed: own pharma growth, avoid insurers until 2026 cost trends are proven.

Narrative: Materials are a monetary-metals trade. XLB is up 10.03% over 20 sessions; gold closed at 5,098.50, up 10.86%, and Freeport is up 10.31% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). Dollar weakness — DXY down 2.32% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11) — is the common driver.
Reported: Linde beat but its shares fell over 2% as 2026 guidance disappointed — industrial gases are a volume business that the metals rally does not help.

EPS Upside Watch: Gold miners: Newmont is up 8.7% over 20 sessions at 124.60 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11), and at current bullion prices margins expand faster than costs, which sets up upward estimate revisions through the next reporting round.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Copper is not confirming: it closed at 5.95, down 0.35% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11), even though it remains the AI data-centre and grid capex metal. Bullish on precious-metal miners, neutral copper until it breaks out.

Narrative: Real estate is a rate-stability trade with a valuation cushion. XLRE is up 4.57% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11) while the 10Y is unchanged over 20 observations at 4.18% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-11), and US REITs ended January at a median 16.2% discount to net asset value.
Reported: NNN REIT announced 2025 results and initial 2026 guidance; net-lease landlords with fixed escalators are the template for steady cash flow in a flat-rate world.
EPS Upside Watch: Net-lease and data-centre REITs: a double-digit discount to NAV lets private buyers arbitrage public prices, which makes take-private M&A the likeliest upside catalyst.

⚡ Breaking Convention: XLRE slipped only 0.09% on payroll day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11) — the market is treating REITs as value, not duration. Bullish while the 10Y holds near 4.18% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-11).

Narrative: Utilities are now a political asset class. XLU is up 4.06% over 20 sessions and NextEra 11.91%, but Constellation is down 16.99% and Vistra 6.57% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11): regulated growth is being bought, merchant power tied to data-centre politics is being sold.
Reported: CMS Energy exceeded its 2025 earnings guidance and raised 2026 adjusted EPS guidance — regulated capex is compounding as planned.

EPS Upside Watch: Regulated utilities with large-load tariffs that make data-centre customers pay for grid upgrades protect rate cases and earnings growth, unlike merchant generators exposed to price caps and political intervention.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Senators introduced the first bipartisan effort to curb utility-bill hikes related to data centres — the AI-power trade now carries regulatory risk. Mixed: own regulated growth such as NEE, avoid independent power producers until the policy shape is clear.

Narrative: European autos face EV write-downs, tariffs and Chinese competition at once. The STOXX autos tracker EXV5 is down 3.01% over five sessions and 2.24% over 20 at 45.84, with Mercedes down 4.92% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).

Reported: Stellantis shares slumped over 20% after a $26.5 billion EV-related writedown; its US listing is down 25.51% over five sessions at 7.62 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). The EV reset has become a balance-sheet event.

EPS Upside Watch: Volkswagen: its China-built Cupra Tavascan was spared EU duties on China-made EVs, cutting the tariff cost on an imported model; VOW3 is down only 0.14% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The VW exemption is also a precedent for Chinese brands to negotiate their way into Europe — the competitive threat rises as the tariff wall softens. Bearish; BMW, down 1.54% over 20 sessions, is the relative defensive (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).

Narrative: Semis are the AI trade that is earning its multiple. SOXX is up 9.03% over five sessions and 8.07% over 20; TSMC's ADR is up 14.84% over five sessions, ASML 13.03% over 20, and Micron rose 9.94% in the prior session to 410.34 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).
Reported: TSMC's January revenue jumped 37% as AI spending marched on, and its board approved a record $45 billion spending package for new fabs — a direct order signal for equipment makers.

EPS Upside Watch: Equipment and memory: the TSMC capex vote feeds ASML and the US tool makers, and Micron's surge shows memory pricing outrunning estimates. NVDA is up 9.11% over five sessions at 190.05 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Memory scarcity taxes the rest of the chain: SMIC says the industry is in 'crisis mode' over the memory crunch. Bullish on memory and equipment, underweight handset and PC chip exposure that must absorb higher memory costs.

Rewarded: The market paid for visible demand and pricing power: CBA's record half sent the shares higher, Spotify jumped on earnings and subscriber growth, and McDonald's beat as value drew traffic. TSMC's January revenue jump kept the AI hardware chain bid.

Punished: Beats without guidance were sold: Cisco fell 7% despite topping estimates. Weak outlooks were punished hard — Molina sank 28% and Dassault Systèmes 18% — and Amazon fell on a miss paired with a $200 billion capex plan.

Pattern: Two filters explain the reactions. Guidance beats the quarter: companies that raise or hold credible outlooks get paid, those that do not are sold regardless of the beat. And AI is a cost line until proven a revenue line — software and capex-heavy platforms are discounted, while hardware where AI already shows up in revenue is rewarded.

Attention into EPS: Applied Materials reports with traders positioned for a large move, the first test of whether TSMC's capex vote converts into tool orders. Coinbase is also on deck, with JPMorgan cutting its target ahead of earnings — a test of how much crypto weakness the stock already discounts.

Playbook: Buy beat-and-raise in hardware, banks and staples retail on the first pullback; sell beat-and-hold in software on the first bounce. Avoid owning capex-heavy platforms into prints unless they quantify AI revenue. Change the call when a guidance-cut stock rallies on the day — that would mark capitulation in the punished cohort.

Attention Gap: Venezuela coverage is dominated by politics, but the operating signal is concrete: Washington issued a license facilitating oil and gas exploration and production in the country. Service companies — which supply rigs, completions and equipment before any new barrel flows — are the first-order beneficiaries, yet the discussion stays on the majors.

Exposure & Risk: Express via SLB, Halliburton and Baker Hughes or the OIH basket, with Chevron as the integrated proxy — CVX is up 13.39% over 20 sessions at 185.82 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). Risks: license reversals, payment risk on a state counterparty, and the EIA's lower-price outlook, which could cap upstream budgets.

Attention Gap: Attention is uniformly negative — the narrative is AI eating software — but JPMorgan strategists say AI fears on software stocks are overblown. Microsoft is down 14.09% over 20 sessions at 404.37 and Oracle 22.31% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11): profitable platforms with proprietary data are being sold alongside seat-based point solutions.

Exposure & Risk: Build slowly in large, cash-generative platforms (Microsoft, Salesforce) or IGV rather than small-cap SaaS. Risks: another model release that broadens the disruption, and credit contagion — Morgan Stanley's warning on a $1.5 trillion credit market means forced selling by lenders is possible. Add only on days when bad news fails to make new lows.

Market Context: Bitcoin's prior completed daily close was 66,991.97, down 2.62% on the day and 25.12% over 20 sessions; ether closed at 1,940.62, down 34.21%, and solana at 79.25, down 38.22% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). The equity proxies are worse: COIN fell 5.73% to 153.20 and is down 39.37% over 20 sessions, MSTR is down 27.12% and IBIT 28.52% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).

New / Most Important: Stress has moved from prices into crypto credit: lender BlockFills suspended withdrawals amid the faltering bitcoin price. The damage is reaching brokers — Robinhood's Q4 revenue missed — and the deeper drawdowns in ether and solana show leverage being flushed from the higher-beta tokens first.

Playbook: Stay underweight; do not buy the dip until bitcoin reclaims the $71,000 area CoinDesk flagged as fresh resistance. Prefer IBIT over COIN and MSTR, where equity and balance-sheet leverage amplify drawdowns. Add only if no other lender follows BlockFills; cut further on a second withdrawal halt or a daily close below 66,991.97 that fails to recover within a week (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).

Rates & Dollar: DXY closed at 96.83, down 2.32% over 20 sessions; TLT is up 1.76% over five sessions at 88.06, HYG is down 0.26% over 20 sessions at 80.83 and LQD 0.05% at 110.70 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). The 10Y at 4.18% and the 30Y at 4.82% are little changed over 20 observations, with the 30Y−10Y spread at +64 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-11). The yuan's climb to its strongest since 2023 amid a report on Treasuries adds an official-sector reason for dollar weakness.

Credit Check: Supply is the story: Alphabet sold almost $32 billion of bonds to fund AI, and investment-grade prices barely moved, with LQD down 0.05% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). The crack is in private markets: Morgan Stanley warns the software selloff may pose a risk to a $1.5 trillion credit market. Public investment-grade credit is fine; private loans to software borrowers are where the marks will come.

Portfolio Implication: Keep credit in investment grade and short-dated high yield; avoid BDCs and private-credit vehicles with heavy software exposure. Hold gold as the dollar-diversification hedge — GLD is up 10.91% over 20 sessions at 467.63 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11) — and add non-US equity, where Europe and Asia lead fund inflows. Change the call if a hot CPI lifts the dollar and real yields together.

What Is Priced: After payrolls rose 130,000, economists expect the Fed to hold through May. The 2Y at 3.52% still yields less than the 3M bill at 3.70% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-11), so the curve continues to price some easing. The delayed report lands on Friday.

Conditional Expression: Hot core print: sell 2Y Treasuries, rotate from homebuilders and small caps into energy and staples retail, and buy the dollar against the euro. Soft print: add duration via TLT, buy homebuilders and IWM, and sell the dollar against the yen. IWM is up only 1.38% over 20 sessions at 264.95 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11), so a soft print has the most room to run there.
